moduli.nome: Today, more than ever, exhibition design is a multifaceted field that can be explored through different interpretative approaches, giving rise to diverse reflections, hypotheses, and theoretical perspectives
Designing an exhibition through architecture means interpreting a curatorial programme by giving it concrete spatial form
It involves organising the selection and sequence of works according to precise spatial relationships within a visitor path designed to generate experience and foster synaesthetic engagement
It means translating the premises of a cultural intention into space through the construction of “visual machines”
The architectural definition of the elements that constitute an exhibition structure is therefore central to the success of any curatorial project

Rather than a simple succession of display panels, an exhibition or museum installation consists of architectural structures specifically conceived for exhibition purposes, in which form and structure coincide

The relationship between staging and abstraction, or conversely between staging and contextualisation, raises a series of questions that can only be addressed through a productive dialogue between curators and designers
Experimentation with modes of communication thus becomes the very substance of exhibition-making
Every exhibition is an intellectual and design adventure that requires direction, precision, and operational rigour: a necessary artifice, at times manifest, at times merely whispered
